title: Two-open locality of finite-window coefficient approximation
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $B\to A$ any map of commutative rings, and $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ a separated finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions]. For a quasi-compact open subscheme $W\subseteq Y$ and a $B$-algebra $D$, write $W_D=W\times_{\operatorname{Spec}B}\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Define the proposition $\mathcal P(W)$ as follows. For every commutative finite type $B$-algebra $D$ with a specified map $D\to A$ over $B$, every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{W_A})$ pseudo-coherent relative to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-derived-category, def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex], and every $a\in\mathbf Z$, there exist a finite type $D$-algebra $D'$ with a factorization $D\to D'\to A$ and $F\in D(\mathcal O_{W_{D'}})$ with bounded coherent cohomology [pqf-def-coherent], and a morphism $\gamma:F\to R\pi_*K$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image], where $\pi:W_A\to W_{D'}$ is projection. Put $q:W_{D'}\to\operatorname{Spec}D'$ and $M=\widetilde A[0]$ on $\operatorname{Spec}D'$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. The morphism
$$\theta:Lq^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}F\longrightarrow R\pi_*K$$
is defined by adjunction [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint] from
$$L\pi^*(Lq^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}F)\simeq L(q\pi)^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\pi^*F\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{W_A}\otimes^{\mathbf L}K\simeq K,$$
using the given $A$-structure and the transpose of $\gamma$ [def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. Its cone [def-weil-triangulated-category] has quasi-coherent cohomology and zero cohomology sheaves in every degree $i\geq a$. There is no flatness requirement on $B\to A$, $D\to A$ or $D'\to A$.
If $U,V\subseteq Y$ are quasi-compact opens and $\mathcal P(U)$, $\mathcal P(V)$ and $\mathcal P(U\cap V)$ hold, then $\mathcal P(U\cup V)$ holds. This is an implication from approximation on the three smaller opens; it does not assert existence of approximations on them.

proof.text: Fix $W=U\cup V$ and an arbitrary $D,K,a$ in $\mathcal P(W)$. Take a finite affine open cover $W=\bigcup_j W_j$, $W_j=\operatorname{Spec}R_j$. Each $R_j$ is finite type over $B$ by the affine-pairs criterion. Thus $S_j=R_j\otimes_B D$ is finite type over $D$; choose a finite polynomial surjection $Q_j=D[x_1,\ldots,x_{s_j}]\twoheadrightarrow S_j$. These charts cover $W_D$ and their $A$-base changes cover $W_A$. The latter have rings $S_j\otimes_D A$. Relative pseudo-coherence, for every integer $m$ and these particular polynomial embeddings, makes their pushforwards $m$-pseudo-coherent for every $m$. All-$m$ pseudo-coherence is absolute pseudo-coherence by its definition. By the affine equivalence, affine pushforward calculation and affine pseudo-coherence criterion, the corresponding $K_j$ restricted to $Q_{j,A}=A[x_1,\ldots,x_{s_j}]$ are pseudo-coherent. The ring $D$ is Noetherian because it is finite type over $B$.

proof.text: Each polynomial restriction of $K_j$ has a bounded-above finite-free representative, hence $H^i(K_j)=0$ above an integer $b_j$. For a nonempty cover take $b=\max_j b_j$; then $H^i(K)=0$ for $i>b$, because its restrictions to the covering opens vanish. If $W$ is empty, take $D'=D$, $F=0$ and $\gamma=0$, which proves the assertion there. For nonempty $W$, start at $N=b+1$ with coefficient ring $D$, $F=0$ and $\gamma=0$. The normalized map is $0\to R\pi_*K$. Affine pushforward is t-exact, so its cone vanishes for all $i\geq N$.

proof.text: The induction invariant at $N$ is a finite type $D$-algebra $E$ factoring to $A$, a bounded-coherent $F$ on $W_E$, and $\gamma:F\to R\pi_*K$ whose normalized scalar-action cone is quasi-coherent and vanishes for $i\geq N$. Keep the fixed covering $W_j$ throughout. At a stage, replace $D$ by $E$, $S_j$ by $R_j\otimes_B E$ and $Q_j$ by $E[x_1,\ldots,x_{s_j}]$. These are Noetherian. The affine equivalence gives $L_j$ from $F$ on this chart. Its cohomology is bounded and finite over $S_j$: coherence implies finite type, and associated sheaves identify finite generators on an affine. The same generators work over the quotient's polynomial source $Q_j$. The Noetherian cohomology criterion gives a bounded-above finite-free $Q_j$-representative $P_j$ of $L_j$ after restriction.

source.place: Agent-written finite downward induction for the two-open prerequisite of the unnumbered Kiehl assertion after Tag 0CSD. Primary descente source WANTED; affine comparison: Tags 08DW, 08DX, 08E7; relative charts: 09UJ, 09VC; obstruction finiteness: 066E, 064K, 064U, 064R, 064S.

proof.text: Every term of $P_j$ is free over $E$ (use the monomial basis of $Q_j$), so $P_j$ is K-flat over $E$ as well as over $Q_j$. Consequently $Q_{j,A}\otimes_{Q_j}P_j=A\otimes_E P_j$ computes the restricted coefficient tensor and is bounded-above finite free over $Q_{j,A}$. Let $\theta_j$ be its extension--restriction counit map to $K_j$ induced by $\gamma$. The affine pullback/tensor formulas identify the restriction of $Lq^*\widetilde A\otimes^{\mathbf L}F$ with $A\otimes_E^{\mathbf L}L_j$: the cancellation is $(S_j\otimes_E^{\mathbf L}A)\otimes_{S_j}^{\mathbf L}L_j\simeq A\otimes_E^{\mathbf L}L_j$. Affine pushforward is restriction of scalars: on a basic open its sections are the localized module, and the affine pushforward resolution lemma identifies this termwise description with derived pushforward. Under these comparisons the transpose defining $\theta$ and the counit defining $\theta_j$ both apply $\gamma$ and multiply by the given scalar in $A$. Thus their cones have the same underlying cohomology after restriction to $Q_j$. This uses no flatness of $E\to A$ or $E\to S_j$.

proof.text: Both source and target of $\theta_j$ are pseudo-coherent over $Q_{j,A}$: for the source use the explicit representative in step 4, for the target use step 1 with the same variables. Apply all-$m$ pseudo-coherence and the cone lemma (source parameter $m+1$, target parameter $m$) to see that $C_j=\operatorname{Cone}(\theta_j)$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent for every $m$. By the invariant and step 4, $H^i(C_j)=0$ for $i\geq N$. In particular it vanishes for $i>N-1$. Top-cohomology finiteness at $m=N-1$ says $H^{N-1}(C_j)$ is a finite $Q_{j,A}$-module. This does not assert finiteness over $A$, which need not be Noetherian.

proof.text: Apply global single-degree coefficient cancellation to $X=W_E$, its fixed affine charts, $F,\gamma,K$ and $n=N-1$. Step 3 supplies its Noetherian and bounded-coherence hypotheses; steps 4--5 supply precisely its polynomial-chart cone hypotheses. The morphism $W_E\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ is separated finite type: the diagonal of $W/B$ is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $Y/B$ (restrict its local quotient presentations), and its finite affine chart rings are finite type. Apply separated finite-type base-change permanence to $W/B$ and $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}B$. The lemma returns a finite type $E$-algebra $E'$ factoring to $A$, and $F',\gamma'$ with normalized cone quasi-coherent and zero for $i\geq N-1$. The base-changed scheme is $(W_E)_{E'}=W_{E'}$. A generating list for $E/D$ followed by one for $E'/E$ generates $E'/D$. This is the invariant at $N-1$.

proof.text: If $a\leq b+1$, perform $b+1-a$ improvements. If $a>b+1$, retain the initial zero model. The result is a finite type $D$-algebra $D'$, a bounded-coherent $F$ on $W_{D'}$ and the required $\gamma$, with exactly the scalar-action normalization specified in the item, and cone zero in all degrees $i\geq a$. This proves $\mathcal P(U\cup V)$. The argument proves this for any quasi-compact $W$; in particular it proves the stated conditional implication. It does not replace derived coefficient tensor by ordinary geometric base change, or assert that the independently chosen approximations on $U$ and $V$ already have isomorphic overlaps.
